sources.title: The Effect of Fuel Injection Location on Supersonic Hydrogen Combustion in a Cavity-Based Model Scramjet Combustor
sources.supported_context: Different hydrogen injection configurations/locations alter mixing, ignition/flame structure and related combustor response.
sources.boundary: Cavity geometry and injection modes differ from the current quasi-1D single-injector model; not a validation dataset for a future P15 sweep.

sources.title: Numerical Investigation of Flow Structures and Combustion Mechanisms with Different Injection Locations in a Hydrogen-Fueled Scramjet Combustor
sources.evidence_type: 3D reacting-flow numerical study with validation context
sources.supported_context: Injector placement is an engineering-relevant variable affecting flame formation, propagation and pressure/combustion behavior.
sources.boundary: 3D cavity/LES/finite-rate-chemistry physics are outside the current teacher quasi-1D algebraic-closure model.

repository_constraint.consequence: A future injector-location study must separate nominal target position from grid-realized source position and should prefer a sampling strategy that does not confound physical location sensitivity with grid-placement offsets.

next_gate: define a cross-grid-comparable position parameterization before CFD
freeze which quantity is held fixed when injector position moves (total fuel flow, phi, fuel state and injection mode)
keep nominal and realized cell-center locations in every point artifact
do not infer universal optimal injector position or cavity-specific flame behavior from the quasi-1D model
